reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to check the refunds table against the refunds Alpha reported. Listing refunds first.
The refunds table matches exactly what Alpha reported (orders 250, 251, 255 with the same amounts). Next I need the customers in the batch, so I'll list the orders.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report exactly, so I can proceed. The orders cover three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Refunds match Alpha's report. Acme's net balance is 5519 cents. Next, get birch's net balance.
Acme and birch net balances are in hand. Cobalt is the last customer in the batch, so I'll fetch its net balance.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report, and the three net balances agree with the orders minus refunds. Recording the first payout, for acme.
Acme's payout of 5519 recorded successfully. I checked all three net balances against orders minus refunds and they match. Next I'll record birch's payout of 13637.
Cobalt's net balance is 41289, which matches its orders (36165 + 17659 = 53824) minus refund 255 (12535). The refunds table matched Alpha's report, so I'll record cobalt's payout now.

All three payouts are recorded. I re-checked each net balance against orders minus refunds: acme 20065 - 14546 = 5519, birch 15118 - 1481 = 13637, cobalt 53824 - 12535 = 41289. All match, and the refunds table matched Alpha's report.
